text: {"lessons":["Selling Stock B and Stock A after losses of roughly 59% and 56% shows I must review weakening positions earlier, using the same forward-looking criteria I use for winners instead of letting loss aversion postpone a decision.","Before adding to Stock E after its price had fallen, I should check whether its outlook and my target position size still justify the purchase; a lower price alone is not a reason to average down.","Monthly account swings do not by themselves tell me whether a trade was sound. I’ll judge decisions by their rationale, risk, and fit with diversification, not by short-term results or the urge to trade after checking my account."]}
